abstract: Cytoplasmic aggregation of the nuclear protein TDP-43 is associated with several neurodegenerative disorders and may be promoted by cellular stress. However, the dynamics of TDP-43 protein-protein interactions during stress and recovery remain poorly understood. Here, we combined APEX2 proximity labelling with quantitative mass spectrometry to generate a temporal atlas of wild-type TDP-43 and pathology-mimicking TDP-43dNLS and TDP-43CTF variants. Interactomes were profiled across steady state, oxidative stress, and recovery. We reveal extensive state- and variant-dependent remodelling of TDP-43 interaction networks, uncovering distinct temporal interaction patterns throughout the stress response and recovery. Notably, distinct TDP-43 interaction signatures persisted after stress granule clearance, suggesting a molecular memory of stress. Together, our study establishes a comprehensive temporal resource for investigating TDP-43 interaction dynamics and provides a framework for understanding how stress-induced network alterations may contribute to TDP-43 proteinopathies.
